 MOBILE, Ala. (NBC 15) — Voters in Alabama House District 25 delivered a historic result Tuesday night, electing Democrat Allison Montgomery over Republican incumbent State Rep. Phillip Rigsby and making Montgomery the state’s first transgender legislator.
 The Associated Press called the race, reporting Montgomery leading Rigsby 53% to 47% with more than 95% of the estimated vote counted, one of three Northern Alabama seats flipped Tuesday night, according to AL.com. 
 Montgomery, a software engineer, campaigned on affordability and divestment from corporate interests. During the campaign, she faced attacks over her gender identity, including one from the chair of the Alabama Republican Party, Republican lawmaker Scott Stadthagen.
 “Republican politicians always point to vague concerns about 'the children' when talking about women like myself, while Republican Rep. Brett Easterbrook gets arrested for soliciting sex with a minor,” Montgomery wrote in a Facebook post. 
 After the race was called, Montgomery posted a victory message on social media, urging attention on the campaign’s approach rather than the historic first.
